thread:
erin: Heads up — customer SynthApps opened a ticket: lots of 503s and high tail latency. They say they're pinned to eu-west but our traces show many requests diverted to us-west and queued. Example request-id: req_0a1b2c3d. Can someone check spillover/autofailover triggers?

sam: I can see alerts from the routing service: region-capacity(eu-west)=EXHAUSTED -> spillover enabled -> target us-west. Alert window started ~1923456700. Any logs with the route decision?

jordan: Also seeing increased queue depth on eu-west node groups. Need the request headers + routing decision log snippet to confirm whether pin header was honored.

erin: Pasting a sample request header we captured: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...
X-Region: eu-west
X-Pin-Region: true
X-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d
```
Routing decision log snippet: `decision=SPILLOVER dest=us-west reason=queue_depth>threshold (203) pool=shared`

natalie: Quick infra check: eu-west prewarm pool at 98% CPU, pending queue length ~220 for 2+ minutes. Autoscaler didn't add nodes because cooldown still active from last scale event. Also there is a reserved_capacity allocation that looks fragmented — a few reserved pools held by other tenants reduced available headroom.

infra-bot: autoscaler-bot: EU-WEST autoscaler cooldown=300s, last_scale_time=1923456500, min_instances=3, max_instances=12. Manual scale-out possible via `infra scale-out eu-west --instances 3`.

sam: Billing check: not a credits issue — billing-bot shows SynthApps has enough credits and no active invoice blocks. So this is routing/policy + capacity.

jordan: Two hypotheses: 1) agent SDK isn't setting a hard pin, so system treats X-Pin-Region as soft-preference and will spillover when SLO risks; 2) token scope mismatch causing routing layer to drop pin header. Erin, can you confirm org metadata for pin config?

erin: In account metadata: `pin_region: true, pin_type: soft`. Oh — we default to soft pins for hosted accounts unless they buy Dedicated/hard-pin add-on. Customer thought pin=true meant hard pin. That mismatch explains expected behavior.

natalie: Repro steps I ran:
1) curl with X-Region: eu-west and X-Pin-Region: true -> service returns 202 normally when eu-west under threshold.
2) artificially push eu-west queue to >200 -> same curl starts returning responses routed to us-west (200ms higher latency) or 503 when us-west overloaded. This is intended: soft pins + spillover to preserve throughput/lower error rates.

sam: Action item: clarify soft vs hard pin in support reply. For hard isolation they must use Dedicated or Private.

erin: Customer is hitting downstream auth checks that validate source region and signature, so spilled requests cause 401s in their infra. They consider this a regression. We need to offer short-term mitigation.

jordan: Short-term mitigation options:
- Option A: Increase eu-west capacity (manual scale-out) to drain queues — quick but may bump costs.
- Option B: Temporarily return 429 when eu-west overloaded instead of spilling to us-west so their client can retry to pinned region. Needs change to failover policy and might increase client-side latency.
- Option C: Provide dedicated endpoint (eu-west.redwood-inference.com) with reserved capacity — guaranteed no spillover.

infra-bot: Note: changing failover from spillover->429 is a config flip `routing/soft_pin_behavior=return_429_on_capacity` and requires a short deploy to routing plane (approx 10m).

billing-bot: If they want Dedicated, rough estimate: 8x A10 GPUs reserved ~ $Xk/mo. I can prepare formal quote; ETA 1 business day.

sam: I'll draft a support reply: explain soft pin, show our logs (decision snippet), include repro and mitigation options (A/B/C), and offer to schedule a call. @billing-bot please attach quote for Dedicated.

erin: I'll follow up with the customer and include a reproducible curl + SDK snippet and their request IDs. Also opening internal ticket to update docs and add KB that clarifies soft vs hard pin semantics. Ticket R-4023 created.

jordan: Long-term: add a route-level contract check that prevents reserved_capacity fragmentation and prioritizes pinned orgs for scale events. Also we should add an event that notifies customers when a soft-pin spillover happens so they get early warning.

natalie: I'll adjust autoscaler cooldown and create a metric-driven escalation to force rapid scale when queue depth > 150 for 30s for pinned orgs. Pushing a PR to infra playbooks.

erin: thanks all. Customer call scheduled in 45m. I'll paste follow-up logs and the exact curl test results after the call. :thumbsup:
